This study introduces a method for guiding 3D surgical instruments during retinal procedures by utilizing a spotlight to project a 2D shadow, which is captured by an endoscope. By employing a depth camera to acquire depth maps, we calculate the 3D positions of both the endoscope and the instrument. These positional data are then used to determine the 2D shadow locations within the endoscope's view. We validate the effectiveness of this approach through experiments conducted on a phantom model.
This paper presents a dual formulation of $F$-polynomials, derived from the dualities existing between cluster algebras and cluster categories.

This work evaluates the feasibility of a passwordless world powered by FIDO2, focusing on the technical and organizational hurdles preventing its full adoption. We explore the potential impact of these limitations on end-users and their ability to leverage FIDO2, ultimately offering recommendations to overcome these barriers and achieve a completely password-free experience.

We examine the framework of Weyl-Wigner quantum mechanics in the context of lattice systems, specifically addressing the harmonic oscillator. Our analysis demonstrates that the phase-space path integral for such lattice models can be constructed by integrating over the phase-space paths of an auxiliary continuum system. Furthermore, we establish a correspondence between the lattice and continuum scenarios, revealing that the lattice harmonic oscillator may be formulated as a continuum Hamiltonian featuring a potential composed of delta functions situated at lattice points.

YouTube serves as a premier platform for content creators, enabling them to share diverse media with a vast audience. Yet, the site's algorithmic architecture is primarily optimized to maximize user engagement, a strategy that often marginalizes creators by obscuring their content. This paper examines YouTube's design through the lens of user agency, revealing how its structural elements foster an environment where creators feel compelled to adopt specific tactics to achieve their goals. The study identifies three distinct creator typologies based on their objectives and strategies: (1) entertainers, who prioritize audience engagement and align well with YouTube's design; (2) educators, who focus on disseminating information but struggle to be seen by their target audience due to the platform's incentives; and (3) activists, who aim to drive social change and are similarly disadvantaged by the system. The research demonstrates that YouTube's design actively pushes entertainers toward behaviors that boost platform metrics, while simultaneously creating significant barriers for educators and activists.

This study examines the trace semantics of a specific class of $\pi$-calculus variants, demonstrating that they possess a finite executable presentation. This class encompasses the asynchronous $\pi$-calculus, which is a broader generalization of the asynchronous $\lambda$-calculus. We establish that trace semantics for this framework is behaviorally complete, implying that every infinite trace corresponds to at least one process. Furthermore, we prove the finiteness of executable presentations within this class, showing that every process admits an equivalent representation as a finite set of infinitely repeated sequences of finite process sequences. These findings extend prior work by Esparza et al. on finite executable presentations, which was originally established for the asynchronous $\lambda$-calculus.

We introduce a method to generate a compact representation for all ordered trees using a single string. This representation is designed to be concise, requiring only a constant number of bits per leaf on average. Furthermore, it allows for the efficient construction of an adjacent representation in O(1) time with high probability.

The sPHENIX experiment at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) is dedicated to investigating the properties of strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma (sQGP) created during heavy-ion collisions. It also aims to analyze high-transverse-momentum (high-pT) jets and heavy-flavor hadrons generated in these events. To achieve this, sPHENIX utilizes a hybrid tracking strategy that combines silicon strip detectors for inner tracks with a magnetic drift chamber for detecting outer tracks. The ACTS software package, a modular and flexible tool for track reconstruction, has been integrated into the sPHENIX software framework. This integration enables the application of state-of-the-art track fitting and vertexing algorithms, facilitating the study of sQGP characteristics, as well as the reconstruction and analysis of jets and heavy-flavor hadrons within the sPHENIX detector system.

This study examines the spatial discretization error inherent in the temporal flux term of discontinuous Galerkin (dG) schemes utilizing temporal interpolation. The analysis covers a broad spectrum of temporal strategies, including constant, linear, and higher-order interpolations across various spatial dimensions. We establish that the jump-term's contribution to the total discretization error scales linearly with the time step size, irrespective of the chosen spatial dimension or temporal strategy. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for sufficiently resolved meshes, this method achieves optimal convergence rates comparable to those of continuous-in-time methods.

A mono-directed signed graph consists of a directed graph augmented by a collection of designated directed edges, referred to as minuses, while the remaining edges are classified as positives. This paper introduces the concept of a circular flow within such a mono-directed signed graph, defining it as an assignment of non-zero values to each edge, where forward and backward flows are treated as distinct. Specifically, an edge labeled a positive receives an integer flow value, whereas an edge labeled a minus is assigned a rational flow that is the additive inverse of its backward direction. We then examine specific circular flows, including the circular 1-flow, the circular 2-flow, and the circular 1/2-flow.

The subset sum problem involves determining whether a specified target can be formed by summing a subset of $n$ integers. While the deterministic algorithms currently known for this task rely on the polynomial-space method by P. B. Wilson, which runs in $O(n^{2.275})$ time, we introduce a novel approach that achieves a superior running time of $O(n^{2.075})$. Our method utilizes the inclusion-exclusion principle combined with the three-sum technique, both of which are executed within polynomial space. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this approach can be streamlined to a running time of $O(n^{1.542})$ by substituting the three-sum component with the fast five-sum algorithm developed by H. L. Bodewig and A. H. M. van der Sluis.

Cell migration is a fundamental process in embryogenesis, yet the mechanisms governing it remain poorly understood. In *Drosophila melanogaster* embryos, hemocytes traverse the yolk to reach the amnioserosa, where they facilitate dorsal closure. Although the yolk acts as a gelatinous medium, hemocytes exhibit anomalous subdiffusive movement within it. This study investigates the physical determinants of this subdiffusion by analyzing the cells' trajectories and the surrounding yolk's rheological properties. We discovered that hemocyte motion is dictated by the interplay between the cell's size and the yolk's viscoelasticity. Specifically, cells smaller than the yolk gel's mesh size undergo normal diffusion, whereas larger cells experience subdiffusion. Furthermore, the cells' ability to migrate depends on the yolk's viscoelastic relaxation time; when this time exceeds the cells' characteristic migration duration, movement becomes arrested. These findings underscore the critical role of mechanical properties in dictating cell behavior during embryogenesis.

This study introduces a semi-supervised speech recognition framework utilizing a contrastive Siamese network. By leveraging a Siamese architecture, the method extracts speaker-specific features from speech data, while employing a contrastive loss function to ensure precise speaker discrimination. This approach enables the system to generate consistent speaker embeddings for identical utterances and distinct ones across varied datasets. Consequently, the model can effectively utilize unlabeled data to enhance performance on labeled tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that this method achieves a 20% relative reduction in Word Error Rate (WER) on the LibriSpeech test set when using 100 hours of labeled data, and a 10% relative reduction when using 400 hours of labeled data, all with an additional 100 hours of unlabeled data.

This study presents a 2021 update to the axial and vector structure functions for inelastic scattering of leptons off nucleons, which are crucial for investigating the nucleon's spin structure. The analysis incorporates the most recent high-precision data from the JLab Hall C experiment, specifically including the $\gamma^* p \to p\pi^0$ reaction. Additionally, it examines the most recent data from HERA regarding the $\gamma^* p \to p\gamma$ process. The investigation also explores the connection between these functions and the generalized parton distributions (GPDs) of the nucleon.

This study addresses the challenge of designing adaptive controls for regime-switching linear quadratic systems where the underlying Markov chain cannot be directly observed. We propose a strategy that combines a filter for estimating the current state with a control policy designed to minimize an estimated value function. We demonstrate that under specific conditions, both the system state and the estimation errors converge to zero, achieving asymptotic stability. Furthermore, the research includes numerical simulations to validate the proposed adaptive control approach.

Active inference serves as a theoretical framework for explaining how the brain minimizes surprise by driving actions. This study introduces a novel extension of branching time active inference tailored for multi-modal and multi-factor scenarios. This approach models the brain's ability to integrate diverse sensory inputs and identify multiple causes for a single event. We demonstrate this approach through an illustrative scenario involving a ball striking a glass window, where the brain must synthesize visual and auditory data to deduce that the window was broken by either a ball, a stick, or both.

We investigate the hydrodynamic framework of cold quark-gluon plasma (cQGP) to analyze the behavior of Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) solitons. Our findings indicate that these solitons remain stable within the cQGP, with their amplitude and width governed by the sound velocity, shear viscosity, and heat dissipation rate. Furthermore, we observe that the velocity of the solitons is independent of the initial velocity of the cQQ.

The concept of isochronicity is defined as all periodic trajectories of a vector field maintaining a consistent period. This study examines two-dimensional systems featuring a singularity with zero eigenvalues, specifically analyzing necessary and sufficient conditions for isochronicity within the linear subspace of such systems. By employing a geometric approach, we characterize linear subspaces exhibiting isochronous behavior and identify those that preclude it.

This paper introduces a novel method for constructing periodic orbits within the Lorenz system. By analyzing similarity between solution curves, we define a similarity signature curve representing time-dependent data. We demonstrate that the Lorenz system's solutions exhibit a specific signature: the curve remains constant over a defined time interval, marking the start of a periodic orbit. We also establish that the signature signature for a periodic orbit is the inverse of its period. Furthermore, we present an algorithm for calculating these curves and apply them to the Lorenz system to successfully formulate three periodic orbits.

This paper demonstrates that the Local Asymptotic Normality (LAN) condition holds for the families of solutions to certain diffusion equations driven by a general Levy process, provided the drift function is sufficiently smooth. Furthermore, we derive optimal convergence rates for the LAN structure in this context and establish the asymptotic normality of the estimator derived from the maximum likelihood method.

We demonstrate that the spectrum of a twisted Laplacian on the universal cover of a Riemann surface is determined by the specific twisted representation utilized and the cohomology class of the twist. This finding enables the identification of the representation from which the twisted Laplacian originates via its spectral properties. Furthermore, we derive a theorem regarding the analytic continuation of the Scattering operator for twisted Laplacians and provide a proof of the existence of twisted eigenfunctions on compact Riemann surfaces.

We introduce FNetAR, a new autoregressive framework that leverages the Fourier transform to model long-range dependencies in sequential data. Our approach utilizes a latent autoregressive architecture where the latent variables are generated via Fourier-transformed tokens, allowing the model to capture long-range patterns efficiently with linear complexity, O(N). This contrasts with autoregressive autoregressive models, which incur quadratic complexity, O(N^2). We demonstrate that FNetAR achieves superior performance on benchmark tasks, including language modeling, time series analysis, and protein design. Specifically, the model outperforms established baselines such as Transformers, GPT-2, and Big-Batch GPT-2, while requiring only 10% of their parameters and training 10x faster.

This study examines the cosmological evolution of Generalized Ghost Pilgrim Dark Energy (GGPDE) within Saez-Ballester's gravitation theory. We analyze the dynamical system governing GGPDE to determine the nature of its fixed points, specifically investigating the conditions under which the universe transitions from a decelerated to an accelerated phase. Furthermore, we demonstrate that GGPDE can adequately describe the universe's expansion history.

This study examines a multi-agent, non-cooperative Mean-Field game involving multiple users and multiple mobile edge computing (MEC) servers. Each user competes to optimize their own service function chain (SFC) by selecting an MEC server and determining the execution frequency for each chain's service functions, with the goal of minimizing total execution cost. Conversely, each server seeks to maximize its profit by setting execution frequencies that balance user payment against execution cost. We introduce a novel, efficient algorithm for users to identify the Mean-Field game equilibrium, demonstrating that under specific conditions, a unique equilibrium exists. Furthermore, we propose a deep reinforcement learning approach to help users converge to this equilibrium more rapidly.

We examine a (1+1)-dimensional Dirac fermion model featuring random masses. By employing a renormalization group approach, we derive the critical exponents for the disorder-relevant operator. Our findings indicate that this fermionic system with random mass exhibits the same universality class as the transverse Ising model in two dimensions.

Although depression is a chronic condition, individuals are not confined to sadness and despair; they also experience happiness. However, the majority of existing research prioritizes negative emotions, largely due to the belief that depression necessitates the identification of distressing events for treatment. This study challenges that assumption by investigating the happy moments of individuals with depression. We introduce a new dataset comprising 1,000 depression patients' diaries, which includes 1,000 entries describing happy events and 1,000 describing negative events. This dataset is annotated with the intensity of happiness and sadness, as well as the specific types of emotions involved. We conducted a comprehensive analysis of the happy events, focusing on the emotions, narratives, and treatments associated with them. Our findings reveal that depression patients experience a wide range of positive emotions, including joy, love, and calmness. Furthermore, the happiness derived from these events is often more intense than that of non-depressed individuals. We also identified that the narratives surrounding these happy events are more positive and that the associated treatments are more effective. This study highlights the importance of acknowledging and supporting the positive aspects of life for individuals with depression.

We examine the impact of isospin breaking in the $Sp(4)$ gauge theory coupled to two-flavor fermions, which serves as the closest simplified model for QCD. Utilizing a combined approach of lattice simulations and the continuum renormalization group, we analyze the chiral phase diagram as a function of quark mass and chemical potential. Our findings indicate that the chiral symmetry breaking transition remains first-order even at zero chemical potential, occurring at a critical quark mass of $m_c \approx 0.11(1) m_g$. Furthermore, we observe that the transition temperature drops significantly as the quark mass increases beyond $m_c$.

We report on the synthesis and characterization of Na$_{4-\delta}$NiTeO$_{6}$, a novel nickel tellurate featuring Ni$^{2+}$ ($S$ = 1) chains. This material crystallizes in a monoclinic structure with space group $C2/c$, where Ni$^{2+}$ ions form zigzag chains within the $bc$ plane. Magnetic susceptibility data reveal a broad maximum at $T_{\rm{max}}$ = 10.5 K, indicating an antiferromagnetic transition. Neutron powder diffraction confirms an antiferromagnetic ground state characterized by a zigzag magnetic order, with a measured Néel temperature of $T_{\rm{N}}$ = 10.5 K. The magnetic moments of the Ni$^{2+}$ ions are determined to be 1.01(2) $\mu_{\rm{B}}$, aligning with the expected spin-only moment. Theoretical analysis using the Heisenberg model, incorporating both intra-chain and inter-chain exchange interactions, supports this zigzag ordering. Furthermore, the magnetic susceptibility is well-described by the Schottky anomaly associated with the Ni$^{2+}$ ground state doublet.

Smart vehicular networks (SVNs) are poised to transform the automotive sector by enabling real-time, high-precision data sharing among vehicles and infrastructure. However, the unverified nature of these data streams introduces significant security and privacy risks, necessitating robust mechanisms to manage trust and uncertainty. This paper introduces a novel framework designed to facilitate trust management and uncertainty reduction within SVN environments. The approach employs a dynamic trust model that evaluates the reliability of vehicles and roadside units (RSUs) based on their historical data quality. Furthermore, the study proposes a probabilistic framework utilizing a Bayesian inference model to assess uncertainty regarding the trustworthiness of vehicles and RSUs. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that this method effectively mitigates uncertainty in trust calculations, thereby enhancing both the accuracy and speed of trust evaluations.

This paper addresses monotone cubic spline interpolation for functions exhibiting strong gradients. The central contribution is the derivation of a straightforward, sufficient condition ensuring the generation of monotone cubics from sampled data points. The proposed method is notably more permissive than existing approaches, including those by Dierckx, King, and Schumaker. Furthermore, we demonstrate that monotone cubics computed via this technique accurately and stably approximate functions with strong gradients, achieving a linear convergence rate in the infinity norm. The study concludes with numerical experiments that validate the method's superior efficiency and the theoretical findings.

This study investigates Taub-NUT spacetimes within a four-dimensional framework featuring negative curvature and a massless scalar field. We derive exact AdS-Taub-NUT solutions to the corresponding Einstein-Maxwell-Scalar equations, noting that these geometries exhibit a specific type of closed timelike curve. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the parameters of the AdS-Taub-NUT solution can be continuously transitioned into those of exact black hole bounces with scalar hair, which are linked to the quantum gravity phenomenon known as the "ER=EPR" conjecture.

This study introduces a new annotation tool designed to help experts categorize audio clips within extensive taxonomies. It addresses key challenges, such as distinguishing between similar audio clips and recalling specific taxonomy entries, by implementing a search module and providing visual examples of past annotations. Additionally, the system offers methods to quickly browse and retrieve previously labeled sounds. It was tested using two large-scale datasets: one comprising over 11,000 categories with more than 100,000 annotations, and the other consisting of roughly 1,000 categories with over 10,000 annotations.

This study introduces a novel approach for analyzing the dynamics of complex systems, termed dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). By applying DMFT to both ecological models and reaction networks, we demonstrate that it yields a tractable, low-dimensional approximation of the system's full dynamics. This approximation is constructed using a self-consistent framework that incorporates the system's internal structure. Our findings indicate that the method accurately reproduces key aspects of the original system's dynamics, such as stability and oscillatory behavior, while simultaneously enabling the calculation of higher-order statistical moments.

We investigate the avalanche size distribution in a simplified model of a dynamical process on a Cayley tree featuring $z$ branches. This system is characterized by a cascade of events where an initial trigger causes a node to flip, subsequently inducing neighboring sites to flip with probability $p$. We demonstrate that the probability of an avalanche affecting a volume $s$ follows a power law, $P(s) \sim s^{-\tau}$, with an exponent $\tau = 1 + \ln(1-z)$. This result aligns with the known scaling exponent $\tau = 5/2$ for the classic avalanche model on a branching random walk.

The perfectly matched layer (PML) is a highly effective technique for absorbing outgoing waves in numerical simulations of wave propagation. Originally developed for time-harmonic problems, the PML has since been extended to time-domain scenarios and various hyperbolic systems. This article presents a concise overview of the PML methodology, focusing on its application to time-domain problems and the wave equation. It further examines the stability of the discretized PML wave equation and the accuracy of its implementation. Additionally, the paper explores the PML's utility in solving other hyperbolic systems, such as the elastodynamic and Maxwell equations.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is rapidly expanding, with billions of devices expected to be connected by 2025. However, the heterogeneous nature of IoT devices and their diverse traffic requirements create significant challenges for network operators. To address this, we introduce a new framework that integrates the Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and IoT architectures. This system leverages the Pub/Sub model to create a flexible, scalable, and efficient mechanism for managing IoT traffic. By utilizing the programmability of SDN, the framework can dynamically adapt to fluctuating traffic patterns. Furthermore, we have developed a control plane algorithm that enables intelligent routing of traffic based on the specific Quality of Service (QoS) needs of individual devices. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves superior scalability, reduced latency, and enhanced resilience against traffic surges compared to existing solutions.

We present a novel analysis of the LkH$\alpha\,330$ protoplanetary disk, utilizing ALMA observations of the $^{12}$CO ($J=2-1$) and $^{13}$CO ($J=2-1$) transitions alongside the C$^{18}$O ($J=2-1$) line. Our findings reveal that the $^{12}$CO emission extends to a radius of 100 au, while $^{13}$CO and C$^{18}$O emissions are confined to 60 and 40 au, respectively. This indicates that the CO isotopologue depletion front is located at a significantly smaller radius than the dust depletion front, suggesting that the CO depletion is driven by a mechanism distinct from dust grain growth. We propose that this phenomenon results from the sublimation of CO ice onto dust grains at the disk's outer edge, which subsequently transports the gas inward. This process is likely triggered by the accretion of a massive planet, which perturbs the disk and facilitates the inward migration of icy dust grains. Furthermore, we observe a correlation between the depletion zones of C$^{18}$O and 10-$\mu$m silicate dust, implying that silicate grains are also responsible for transporting CO ice inward. Hydrogen networks are essential for decarbonizing the European energy landscape, yet their economic viability remains uncertain. This study examines the impact of hydrogen infrastructure on the cost of decarbonization across three distinct scenarios: a baseline with no network, a scenario with a limited regional network, and a scenario with a continent-wide network. The analysis reveals that while a limited network offers significant benefits, a comprehensive continent-wide structure is indispensable for achieving deep decarbonization. Furthermore, the study highlights that the optimal deployment of hydrogen networks is highly sensitive to the specific characteristics of the hydrogen demand.

This study examines the detection of anisotropy in solar travel times using horizontal magnetic fields (HMFs) located in the upper subsurface. We demonstrate that HMFs can be utilized to identify anisotropic propagation, with the direction of this anisotropy aligning with the orientation of the horizontal magnetic field. Furthermore, the magnitude of this anisotropy is proportional to the strength of the horizontal magnetic field. These findings are supported by both numerical simulations and observations from the Solar Orbiter spacecraft.

Squeezed light serves as a vital resource for quantum metrology and computing, yet its generation in integrated photonic platforms is typically hindered by fabrication imperfections that degrade performance. This work demonstrates that topological protection can overcome such challenges by enabling robust, topologically-protected squeezed light generation on integrated photonic chips. We introduce a photonic topology-engineered chip featuring a topologically protected mode, which facilitates the efficient production of squeezed light via spontaneous four-wave mixing. Our results indicate that topologically protected squeezed light exhibits resilience against fabrication errors, outperforming conventional chiral photonic structures. Furthermore, we show that the topologically protected mode can be seamlessly integrated with other topologically protected modes to facilitate efficient, topologically protected light generation. This work highlights the potential of topological photonics for the realization of robust, topologically protected squeezed light generation on integrated photonic chips.

This study addresses time-optimal trajectory planning for a quadcopter, a problem known for its complexity due to the system's high-order dynamics. To overcome these challenges, we introduce a technique that simplifies the dynamics into a low-order model, enabling the use of classical control methods. This approach yields a smooth, closed-form solution that facilitates the rapid generation of time-optimal trajectories for various flight tasks.

This study examines the algebraic structure of additive conjucyclic codes, which are F_q-linear within finite field F_{q^2} of characteristic p where p is a prime and q is a positive integer divisible by p. We establish the algebraic framework for these codes, demonstrating that they constitute the ideal of a specific commutative ring with identity. Furthermore, we outline the structural characteristics of these codes and provide a full classification of them.

This report outlines the Topical Group on Career Pipeline and Development (CommF2) within the Community Engagement Frontier (CEF) at Snowmass 2021. It details the group's objectives, structure, and the specific subjects of its discussions. Furthermore, it presents survey findings regarding both the quantity and quality of CEF programs, offering recommendations for future initiatives. The report also addresses key topics concerning career trajectories and professional growth for experimental particle physicists, including mentoring frameworks, leadership cultivation, and the development of essential soft skills. In addition, it explores the need for diverse and inclusive programs, the expansion of workforce opportunities into the private sector, and the creation of sustainable career pathways for underrepresented groups. The document also covers emerging fields of interest such as community building, the development of essential soft skills, and the impact of artificial intelligence and machine learning on the field.

This work details the measurement of $W$ boson polarization derived from top quarks produced in proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 8 TeV. The analysis utilizes 20.2 fb$^{-1}$ of data recorded by the ATLAS detector at the LHC. The study focuses on $t\bar{t}$ events characterized by a single isolated charged lepton, at least one jet, and at least one $b$-tagged jet. The differential cross-section is determined as a function of the top quark's rapidity, utilizing the angular distribution of the top quark decay products. The observed polarization is found to be consistent with the Standard Model prediction, yielding a measured value of $0.99 \pm 0.07$.

This study revisits the light-cone distribution amplitudes (DAs) of the $D$-meson, specifically focusing on the longitudinal twist-2 and twist-3 components. By employing the QCD factorization framework, we examine the evolution of the twist-2 and 3 longitudinal light-cone DAs, alongside the evolution of the twist-2 transverse DA. Our findings indicate that the longitudinal twist-2 DA is governed by the decay constant $f_D$ and the twist-3 DA by the quark condensate $\langle 0|\bar{q}(0)| D(p)\rangle$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the twist-2 transverse DA is determined by the light-cone distribution function $\rho_D$.

The $k$-th power hypergraph of a graph $G$, denoted $G^{\otimes k}$, is defined such that its vertices correspond to those of $G$, while its edges consist of all $k$-sets of vertices forming a complete subgraph in $G$. This paper determines the spectrum of $G^{\otimes k}$ for any graph $G$ and all positive integers $k$. Additionally, we examine the sign structure of signed subgraphs within $G$ and compute the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix.

This study investigates the localisation of individual user terminals (UTs) within the Starlink satellite constellation. Leveraging the system's extensive network, UTs can access a vast number of beacons, enabling them to determine position through signal measurements. However, due to the non-linear relationship between these measurements and the resulting geometric configuration, the associated localisation errors are often significant. To address this, the paper introduces a novel cooperative localisation framework wherein UTs exchange data to refine the positional accuracy of one another. The authors derive analytical performance limits for this method, specifically the Cramér–Rao lower bound (CRLB), by applying the error propagation law to the covariance matrix of the estimated positions. We report the detection of transit timing variations (TTVs) in the hot Jupiter XO-3b, which manifest as a sinusoidal pattern with a period matching the planet's orbital period. This signal is too weak to be explained by the gravitational influence of other bodies, indicating it stems from tidal evolution. The observed pattern aligns with tidal models that account for the planet's migration from an eccentric orbit to a circular one. The data support an eccentricity of $e = 0.11 \pm 0.03$ at the onset of this migration. The results are consistent with tidal evolution driven by the planet's interaction with its host star, specifically through tidal dissipation within the planet characterized by a quality factor of $Q_p = 10^5$.

The 21-cm global experiment faces a significant hurdle in separating the faint cosmological signal from the much stronger foregrounds. A primary source of error is the coupling between the receiver and antenna, which generates "noise waves" that mimic this signal. These are produced by reflections of the low-frequency galactic background and interstellar turbulence off the receiver's components. To address this, we introduce a Bayesian framework for calibrating these noise waves. This method utilizes a prior distribution derived from the known characteristics of the galactic sky to identify and remove these artifacts. We demonstrate the approach using data from the Murchison Widefield Array (MWA), showing that it successfully eliminates the noise waves. Furthermore, we highlight how this technique can be adapted for future instruments like the Square Kilometre Array Low Frequency (SKA-Low) and the Hydrogen Epoch of Reionization Array (HERA).

This work examines the quantum deformation of the isomorphism connecting the cohomology of Grassmannians to those of flagmannerians, utilizing the formalism of quantum bundles developed by A. Kato. We demonstrate that this extended correspondence holds true for the $n$-point genus-$g$ Gromov–Witten theory within a projective bundle. Furthermore, we establish an isomorphism between the cohomology groups of the flagmannerians and the Grassmannians in the context of the quantum deformation of the Grassmannians.
We establish prime number theorems that are uniformly valid throughout a highly extended region.

This study introduces a statistical framework utilizing natural cubic splines to analyze clinical trials for Alzheimer's disease, specifically targeting longitudinal biomarkers. The approach accommodates both complete and missing-at-random data, with the latter addressed via an augmented data framework. By integrating baseline covariates into the spline model, we estimate treatment effects on biomarkers. We further examine the influence of treatment effect heterogeneity by adding an interaction term between the spline basis and treatment covariate; this allows for the identification of specific ranges where treatment benefits are most pronounced. The analysis includes methods for hypothesis testing regarding these interactions and proposes a new metric to define the corresponding subgroups. Simulation results demonstrate the proposed method's performance in recovering treatment effect patterns and locating optimal subgroups, with an application to data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative illustrating the method's utility.

The surge in private vehicle ownership has exacerbated traffic congestion and parking shortages, particularly in urban centers. To address this, smart parking systems utilize IoT technologies to provide real-time parking availability data to drivers. However, maintaining a continuous stream of accurate, up-to-date information remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a crowdsourcing algorithm designed to leverage data from private vehicles to enhance smart parking infrastructure. By utilizing GPS and Bluetooth beacons, the system tracks the real-time locations of participating vehicles. When a vehicle exits a parking spot, a nearby Bluetooth-enabled vehicle in the same vicinity can verify the vacancy. This verification process is further validated by cross-referencing data from multiple sources, including vehicle owners, other users, and other GPS points. The proposed approach is evaluated through a simulation that demonstrates the algorithm's effectiveness.

The effectiveness of optimizers in minimizing flat versus sharp minima within neural networks has been a subject of extensive research. While recent findings indicate that these methods often fail to produce flat minimums in overparameterized neural networks, this study investigates the specific conditions under which they do succeed. We demonstrate that, for a particular class of networks, both SGD and sharp-to-blunt transitions can achieve the minimizers of the training loss function. However, the resulting solutions differ in their landscape geometry: SGD tends to converge to shallower minima, whereas the Adam optimizer often reaches deeper minima. We further prove that, outside this specific class of networks, neither optimizer reliably secures flat minimums at the training solution.

This paper introduces a reflective, parametric frequency-selective power limiter (FPSL) designed for integration into phased array systems. The device achieves a passband insertion loss below 1 dB, exhibits reflective operation with greater than 30 dB of out-of-band isolation, and maintains a power threshold under 1 mW. The design utilizes a planar resonator as a frequency-selective filter, coupled with a reflective transmon qubit to facilitate signal limiting.

This study introduces a novel SEIRS epidemiological framework for analyzing the COVID-19 pandemic, specifically addressing the extreme scenario where acquired immunity is absent. In this case, individuals transition from Susceptible (S) directly to Exposed (E) at a rate of $\mu$, bypassing an infectious stage. Unlike traditional SEIR models, this approach integrates a compartment for those who have recovered from the disease (R). The model posits that the progression from Exposed to Infectious occurs at a constant rate of $\mu$, while the transition from Infectious to Recovered follows a rate of $\mu$, with the infectious period being defined by the reciprocal of this rate. The model also accounts for the loss of immunity at a constant rate of $\mu$, transforming individuals from the Susceptible category to the Exposed category. The model's dynamics are governed by a system of four ordinary differential equations, which are derived from the model's assumptions and solved analytically. The resulting solutions provide a clear understanding of the model's behavior and the impact of the parameters on the system's dynamics. The model's predictions are validated against the observed data from the first wave of the COVID-19 pandemic in Italy, demonstrating the model's ability to accurately describe the system's behavior and the impact of the parameters on the system's dynamics. Word embeddings are widely utilized in natural language processing, yet their optimal training context remains under-explored. This study investigates how the extent of contextual information influences embedding quality by evaluating three distinct context definitions: word identity, word identity paired with part of speech, and word identity coupled with surrounding context. We assess performance across multiple downstream tasks, including word similarity, word sense disambiguation, and word classification. Our findings indicate that incorporating contextual data significantly enhances the accuracy of these downstream applications.

This study investigates the formation of clusters within high-intensity random geometric graphs (RGGs) in $\mathbb{R}^d$ where node counts approach infinity. We establish that, for sufficiently high node density, the node count within any given $k$-cluster adheres to a Poisson distribution. We further derive a closed-form expression for the expected number of $k$-clusters and analyze the asymptotic behavior of these clusters as node density increases.

We introduce a novel method for deriving analytical solutions to Euler's equation in the context of rotating stars. This approach utilizes a Lagrangian framework to model the fluid's motion, thereby reducing the problem to solving a system of coupled partial differential equations. We establish a correspondence between our derived Lagrangian solutions and the Hertzian solution, effectively parameterizing Hertzian solutions using the Lagrangian variables. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Lagrangian solution represents a specific instance of the Hertzian solution.

The study investigates the Lemaître-Tolman-Bondi (LTB) spacetime within the Palatini $f(R)$ gravity framework, where the Ricci scalar $R$ is a function of the Ricci scalar invariant. By employing a specific functional form for $f(R)$, the authors derive the corresponding field equations. These equations are subsequently reformulated into a dynamical system to analyze the evolution of the universe. The findings indicate that the model exhibits a rich variety of cosmological behaviors, including an initial Big Bang singularity, an accelerated expansion phase, and a future Big Rip scenario.

We demonstrate that any $N$-partite system, where $N \geq 3$, can exhibit a robust quantum nonlocal effect known as strong quantum nonlocality. This phenomenon involves a set of linearly dependent, nonlocal product states that cannot be distinguished via local measurements alone. Our construction utilizes a group-theoretic approach to generate these nonlocal product states, which are inherently linearly dependent. Furthermore, we prove that the maximal number of such product states within a given support is achieved when they form a group under multiplication.

This study introduces a new approach for predicting human visual attention within web pages, utilizing a combination of raw eye-tracking data and computer vision techniques. The proposed method is designed to be more efficient and accurate than existing solutions, specifically by predicting attention for short intervals of eye fixation. The core of the approach involves a novel algorithm that segments raw saccade and fixation data into short-span windows, which are then processed by a convolutional neural network (CNN) to generate attention maps. The model was trained using eye-tracking data from 100 participants navigating a website, with its performance validated against an independent dataset of 50 subjects viewing the same site. The results demonstrate that this short-span window strategy yields higher accuracy in predicting visual attention compared to traditional methods that analyze long sequences of saccades and fixations.

This paper introduces the first experimental validation of a transmissive reconfigurable intelligent surface (TR-RIS) for next-generation (6G) communications. By utilizing a TR-RIS, we can manipulate the phase of radio frequency (RF) signals passing through a passive array of elements, thereby enabling precise control over transmitted signals. We present a fully programmable TR-RIS prototype, which is then integrated into a wireless testbed to evaluate its performance. The study examines the impact of RIS-induced phase shifts on the received signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and compares this against a baseline system without RIS. The results confirm that the TR-RIS significantly enhances SNR, achieving a maximum gain of 10 dB. Furthermore, we demonstrate the TR-RIS's adaptability by configuring it to optimize SNR across various channel conditions. The paper concludes by discussing the key advantages and potential applications of this innovative technology.

Offline reinforcement learning (RL) involves optimizing a policy using static datasets, a scenario where the agent cannot interact with the environment. While recent research has largely focused on achieving sample-efficient algorithms for offline RL, the majority of these methods are restricted to tabular or linear function spaces. In contrast, this paper re-examines the application of linear function approximation within the linear programming (LP) framework for RL. We introduce a novel algorithm that attains a minimax-optimal regret of $\tilde{O}(d\sqrt{H}N^{1/3}\epsilon^{-1/3})$, where $d$ denotes the dimensionality of the feature space, $H$ is the episode length, and $N$ represents the size of the data collection. This result improves upon prior work by eliminating the inverse polynomial dependency on the number of samples. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our regret bound is nearly optimal, as it matches the theoretical lower bound up to a logarithmic factor.

This note demonstrates that the free monoidal category possessing the colimit property is the free topological space, achieved by applying the nerve construction. Consequently, the equivalence between the homotopy theory of topological spaces and the study of monoidal categories under homotopy is established.

The object's bolometric luminosity-to-mass ratio ($L/M$) is $1.1 \times 10^6$ erg s$^{-1} M_{\odot}^{-1}$, placing it among the most efficient black holes known. This paper examines planar three-body configurations where one body resides on the straight line segment connecting the other two. We demonstrate that for any initial conditions placed in such a setup, the resulting motion remains globally defined and does not encounter any singularities.

Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Microscopy (FLIM) is a powerful, non-invasive technique that quantifies the local microenvironment of fluorophores, thereby enabling the study of cellular functions and processes. This study introduces a deconvolution method to enhance the resolution of FLIM images, which are inherently degraded by optical aberrations. The approach involves modeling the system's point spread function (PSF) and the system's response function (SRF) to deconvolve the recorded data. This process is achieved by applying the Wiener filter to the Fourier domain, which simultaneously suppresses noise and optical aberrations. The efficacy of this method is demonstrated through both synthetic and experimental datasets.

Product search is a fundamental component of e-commerce, yet existing methods often fail to adequately model user behavior, resulting in suboptimal search outcomes. To address this, we introduce a new product search framework that integrates user behavior modeling with graph convolution for personalized results. Specifically, we develop a graph convolutional network (GCN) to capture user behavior, utilizing a product knowledge graph to encode product attributes and relationships. We then propose a novel scoring function that leverages these GCN-based user representations alongside product embeddings to generate precise search rankings. Empirical evaluations on a real-world e-commerce dataset demonstrate that our approach significantly surpasses current state-of-the-art techniques.

Unsupervised graph embedding seeks to map graph nodes into a low-dimensional space while maintaining their intrinsic manifold structure. While existing approaches have demonstrated significant potential, they often rely on labeled nodes or fail to adequately capture the underlying geometry of the data. To address these limitations, we introduce a novel framework for unsupervised graph representation that explicitly models the manifold structure of attributed graphs. Our method integrates deep neural networks with manifold learning to simultaneously optimize for both geometric and semantic node information. Specifically, we utilize a deep neural network to learn a manifold structure that preserves node semantics, while employing a semi-supervised learning strategy to refine the manifold learning process. Furthermore, we develop a novel loss function designed to simultaneously minimize the geodesic distance between nodes and maximize their Euclidean separation. Extensive experiments on various benchmark datasets confirm that our approach outperforms current state-of-the-art methods.

This study introduces a novel two-stage genetic algorithm (GA) designed to optimize non-orthogonal sequences for use in massive connectivity grant-free systems. The initial stage employs a GA to generate random sequences, while the subsequent stage utilizes a simulated annealing (SA) algorithm to refine these sequences. This approach is specifically tailored for systems where the base station lacks prior knowledge of user data. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through simulations, which show that it achieves a lower bit error rate (BER) compared to existing state-of-the-art designs.

Compressed sensing (CS) is a technique used to recover high-dimensional signals from a reduced set of linear measurements. In encoder-blind CS, the encoder is responsible for creating a sparse signal from an input vector, while the decoder is tasked with reconstructing the original input from these compressed measurements. This paper introduces a novel class of encoder-blind CS problems, where the encoder generates a sparse signal by multiplying the input vector with a sparse matrix containing a fixed number of ones per row. We demonstrate that the decoder can recover the input vector with high probability from these sparse measurements, provided the number of ones per column is small. Furthermore, we establish a lower bound on the number of ones per row, showing that the proposed approach is optimal.

This paper introduces a novel method for enhancing the robustness of deep neural networks by integrating adversarial training with random transformations. The proposed approach involves applying these random transformations to the input data, performing adversarial training on the resulting transformed data, and subsequently training the model on the original, untransformed inputs. We demonstrate that this technique yields superior performance compared to conventional adversarial training methods, particularly in the face of distributional shifts. Furthermore, the method exhibits strong generalization capabilities across various tasks, including image classification, domain adaptation, and out-of-distribution generalization.

This paper establishes that any 2-local inner derivation acting on the Jordan ring of self-adjoint matrices defined over a commutative involutive ring corresponds strictly to a derivation. Furthermore, it demonstrates that any such 2-local derivation is also a local derivation derived from a single inner source.

The impact of gravitational lensing on the Berry phase of a Dirac monopole is examined. It is demonstrated that the phase acquired by an adiabatic particle orbiting this monopole behaves as if it were lensed. Furthermore, we analyze how lensing influences the gravitational magnetic flux and the resulting Einstein-Nordenberg term within the phase formula.

This study examines the properties of compactons and solitary waves within two-component Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs), specifically investigating how the spin-orbit (SO) density dependence influences their existence. We demonstrate that BEC compactons can be established by applying a suitable magnitude of the SO coupling parameter. Furthermore, we reveal that SO compactons possess a distinct structure characterized by a flat central region, contrasting with the smooth profiles of BEC solitary waves. We also analyze the impact of varying the SO density dependence on the spatial distribution of compactons and their solitary waves. Finally, we explore the dynamic behavior of these compactons under different SO coupling strengths.

The $\Lambda_c(2595)^+$ and $\Lambda_c(2625)^+$ are two $\Lambda_c$ resonances with masses near 2.6 GeV, both possessing $1/2^-$ parity and spin. This study investigates whether they represent a single resonance doublet by applying heavy quark spin symmetry (HQSS) to their couplings with $D^* \bar K$ and $D^* \bar K$ states. The analysis reveals that the $\Lambda_c(2595)^+$ and $\Lambda_c(2625)^+$ cannot be classified as a HQSS doublet. Furthermore, the study examines the $1/2^-$ and $3/2^-$ $S$-wave $\Lambda_c$ states, suggesting that the $\Lambda_c(2880)^+$ and $\Lambda_c(2880)^+$ are candidates for a HQSS doublet.

This paper establishes the Whitney equivalence for orbit spaces arising from the action of a compact Lie group on a manifold. Specifically, we demonstrate that for a compact Lie group $G$ acting on a manifold $M$, the mapping space $\mathcal{C}^k_M/G$ of $G$-equivariant $C^k$ maps into a closed, submanifold $M$ invariant under $G$, serves as a Whitney approximation of all $G$-invariant $C^k$ functions defined on $M$.

This study outlines a strategy for detecting Axion-Like Particles (ALPs) at high-energy muon colliders, focusing on a scenario where the muon collider serves as the primary facility for electroweak physics. We examine the production and decay of ALPs, which are generated in association with the Standard Model and subsequently detected through their decays into various final states. Our analysis covers the entire parameter space, including the pseudoscalar limit, and evaluates the projected sensitivities of the muon collider against other proposed facilities. Additionally, we address the specific challenges posed by muon decay and the development of advanced detector technologies required to achieve these goals.

Contemporary data-centric workloads are characterized by their diversity and complexity, making it challenging to achieve high performance through a single optimization strategy. To address this, we introduce MetaSys, an open-source system designed for metadata management that facilitates the implementation and evaluation of cross-layer optimizations. MetaSys enables researchers to create, assess, and compare various optimization techniques, including those that transcend specific hardware or software components. The system supports the development of custom optimizations and provides a library of pre-built examples, such as cache coherence protocols and data compression algorithms. We demonstrate MetaSys's utility by implementing three distinct cache coherence protocols, each achieving up to 1.5x performance gains. Furthermore, we apply these optimizations to a memory hierarchy featuring cache compression, resulting in up to 2.5x improvements in overall system performance.

This study introduces transfer learning strategies for image classification that leverage synthetic data and Siamese networks. We evaluate these approaches against a state-of-the-art baseline using the CIFAR-10 and ImageNet datasets, demonstrating that our methods achieve competitive performance. Furthermore, our analysis indicates that these methods offer significant advantages when the source and target datasets are small.

This paper examines a specific class of singular, anisotropic, and spatially non-homogeneous $N$-dimensional elliptic systems with $N\geq 2$, which are subject to a specific growth condition. The study establishes the existence of a positive weak solution for these systems.

Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are a dominant approach for sequential data processing, yet they often struggle with long-term dependencies due to vanishing gradients. This paper introduces Fourier recurrent units (FRUs), a novel architecture designed to overcome these limitations. By leveraging Fourier series to model temporal patterns, FRUs can capture long-term dynamics with high precision. We demonstrate that the gating mechanism in FRUs is straightforward to implement and that the resulting vanishing gradient problem can be mitigated by applying Fourier series approximation. Furthermore, we provide a theoretical analysis of FRUs, demonstrating their capacity to learn long-term dependencies. Empirical evaluations across various tasks confirm that FRUs outperform standard RNN variants in modeling extended temporal relationships.

This paper investigates the problem of identifying the optimal policy in Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) by defining the goal as locating a policy that yields the maximum expected return. We introduce a novel framework for MDP navigation, modeled as a sequential game between a navigation agent and an adversary. In this setting, the agent selects actions that incur costs, aiming to locate the globally optimal policy, while the adversary manipulates the MDP's transition dynamics to obstruct this search. We establish a theoretical upper bound on the number of steps required for the agent to locate the optimal policy with high probability, even against the worst-case scenario. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the agent can achieve this identification using a number of steps that scales polynomially with the MDP's size.

We introduce a novel dual-wake injection method for producing high-brightness, linearly polarized attosecond electron bunches. This approach utilizes a first accelerator structure to generate an ultrashort electron slice and a second structure to induce transverse emittance through a kick. The dual-wake injection method offers several advantages, including the ability to create a polarized attosecond electron beam with superior brightness and a significantly reduced longitudinal length. Furthermore, the dual-wake injection method is highly flexible, allowing for the customization of the final beam's length and transverse emittance.

We examine the emergence of complexity in astrophysical settings, ranging from primordial nucleosynthesis to the formation of life. Our analysis reveals a consistent pattern: as complexity increases, the corresponding entropy decreases. This perspective offers a unified framework for understanding thermodynamic principles across various fields of physics and their connections to quantum mechanics and gravity.

This study examines the advantages and constraints of utilizing open-source repositories and artificial intelligence to map the evolution of climate change research, specifically to support evidence-based R&D policy formulation. We analyzed 1.2 million publications from Scopus and arXiv, employing an AI-driven method to identify and track the evolution of 100 climate-related research clusters. The findings indicate that open repositories and AI offer significant potential for monitoring and analyzing vast research landscapes, yet they also present specific limitations. Consequently, while the study provides insights into the shifting focus of climate research, it highlights the necessity for rigorous validation of AI-generated findings before they inform public policy.

Android's dominance in the mobile market has spurred a surge in applications, including those developed in C/C++ via the NDK. While NDK offers superior performance for compute-intensive tasks, it introduces side-channel vulnerabilities that facilitate security breaches. Addressing this, we introduce ASVAAN, a framework designed to automatically detect side-channel attacks in NDK-based apps. By leveraging the NDK's native APIs, ASVAAN precisely locates vulnerable code sections and pinpoints specific operations responsible for side-channel leaks. We evaluated ASVAAN against 11 open-source NDK applications, successfully identifying vulnerabilities in 10 of them. Furthermore, we validated ASVAAN's efficacy by detecting a side-channel attack in a real-world NDK-based banking application.

Blockchain technology has gained significant traction for facilitating secure, decentralized, and transparent transactions. Ethereum, a prominent blockchain platform, enables the development of decentralized applications (dApps) and smart contracts, which are self-executing programs with predefined terms. This study examines Ethereum's transaction data to analyze the ego networks of its most active participants. We categorize these networks based on transaction types, specifically focusing on those involving smart contracts and those that are contract-less. Our analysis reveals that the network's structural and dynamic characteristics vary significantly depending on whether the activity involves smart contracts. Furthermore, we identify that the behavior of these networks is driven by diverse groups of users, each exhibiting distinct patterns.

We report on the observation of quantum oscillations in a two-dimensional electron system (2DES) located at the LaAlO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$ (LAO/STO) interface, induced by optical excitation. The study utilizes a high-quality LAO/STO heterostructure featuring a 30 nm LaAlO$_3$ layer, where the 2DES is situated at the interface. While the system remains insulating in the dark, optical illumination triggers a metal-insulator transition, resulting in a low-resistance metallic state. At low temperatures, this illuminated metallic phase exhibits quantum oscillations with a period corresponding to the filling of a single Landau level. The oscillation frequency is consistent with a carrier density of $1.1 \times 10^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$, matching the carrier density measured in the dark. Furthermore, the oscillation amplitude displays a dependence on the magnetic field that aligns with the Lifshitz-Kosevich model, indicating that the oscillations arise from the quantization of the 2DES's cyclotron motion.

This work presents a new, efficient method for cut-elimination within the classical linear logic system BV, which utilizes a single, concise operation. This approach is highly effective for both the classical logic BV and linear logic, demonstrating superior performance compared to standard cut-elimination. We achieve this by leveraging the structural properties of BV proofs and interactions, facilitated by our novel method of "shifting," which bypasses the need for explicit exponent rules. This technique allows us to bypass traditional mechanisms like promotion and abstraction, effectively treating BV proofs as trees of logical atoms. Consequently, we establish a direct correspondence between the number of shiftings and the size of the proof, proving that the number of shiftings required for cut-elimination is linear relative to the cut-rank. This result provides a new, linear-time cut-elimination procedure for BV, offering a significant improvement over previous methods.

The Gaudin model, characterized by a set of commuting Hamiltonians, is a significant area of study in mathematical physics. In this work, we introduce a new family of commuting operators linked to the Ding-Iohara-Miki algebra and investigate their connection to quantum affine algebras.

We introduce a novel photometric redshift algorithm designed for deep, wide-field surveys, utilizing data from the W-CDF-S and ELAIS-S1 fields. This method employs a spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting technique that incorporates forced photometry from 0.36 to 4.5 microns, leveraging the extensive wavelength coverage of the WFC3/IR instrument. Our approach employs a Bayesian framework to estimate redshifts, with the Bayesian posterior probability distribution serving as the basis for calculating the photometric redshift, its uncertainty, and outlier rejection. We demonstrate that this forced photometry method significantly enhances redshift accuracy compared to broadband photometry alone. Specifically, the median redshift error for forced photometry is 0.015, a substantial improvement over the 0.021 error observed with broadband photometry. This reduction in error is primarily driven by the inclusion of near-infrared bands, which are essential for identifying the 4000 Å break and accurately determining redshifts for galaxies with $z > 1.5$.

This study introduces a novel Bayesian decision support system designed to aid energy system planners in selecting optimal investment strategies. The framework integrates two key probabilistic elements: a stochastic optimization model that determines the best long-term plans for the energy system, and a probabilistic forecasting model that estimates the likelihood of various future scenarios. The scenario probability model leverages machine learning to predict the probability distributions of critical variables, such as electricity demand and renewable energy production costs, by utilizing historical data. The resulting stochastic optimal power flow model evaluates the robustness of investment portfolios against these predicted scenario distributions. Ultimately, the two models operate iteratively, with the probability model refining its predictions based on feedback from the optimization model, thereby enhancing the overall quality of the decision-making process.

This finding is significant because it highlights the inherent simplicity of the two-electron wavefunction, even when accounting for entanglement between spatial and spin degrees of freedom. We investigate a dark matter model featuring a non-abelian gauge symmetry $SU(2)_D$ that binds two Dirac fermions into a vector particle. This particle serves as the dark matter candidate and generates significant contributions to the leptonic $g-2$ anomalous magnetic moments. We analyze the model's parameter space, focusing on the constraints from dark matter relic density, direct detection experiments, and LHC searches. Our findings indicate that the model can account for the observed dark matter abundance while simultaneously resolving the $g-2$ anomaly for the muon.

The surge in frequency and severity of extreme weather events has intensified the need for rapid, accurate forecasting of coastal flooding. This study introduces a surrogate model grounded in physics and neural operators to predict tide-induced water levels, utilizing a dataset derived from the hydrodynamic model Delft3D5. By employing Fourier neural operators (FNO) to map initial conditions to sea surface elevations, the model achieves a prediction accuracy of 99.9% for tide heights, with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.01 m. Furthermore, the model demonstrates the capacity to forecast flood events across various scenarios, including different tidal periods, storm surge heights, and storm surge heights. This approach offers a significant speedup of 1000x compared to traditional hydrodynamic simulations, enabling the creation of a fast, high-fidelity digital twin for Earth's coastlines.

The BeyondPlanck and Cosmoglobe initiatives represent two critical open-science endeavors dedicated to analyzing Planck data. These collaborations prioritize transparency and reproducibility by employing open-source software, maintaining an accessible and transparent version control system, and providing comprehensive, publicly available code documentation. This paper details the version control strategies and documentation frameworks adopted by these groups, while also addressing efforts to standardize software interfaces and data formats. Furthermore, we examine the long-term preservation of data and software, emphasizing the critical role of proper citation in ensuring appropriate credit and fostering the sustainable reuse of scientific resources.

Reaction-diffusion systems are frequently employed to model biological pattern formation, yet their standard reaction-diffusion formulation is Turing unstable when coupled into a network. This study demonstrates that introducing a finite propagation speed into such a networked system restores Turing instability, enabling the generation of these patterns. We further show that the network's topology dictates pattern formation, with the system's dynamics converging toward the behavior of the corresponding network Laplacian.

We introduce a framework for Yang-Mills theory that closely resembles a quasiclassical description. This is accomplished by mapping the Yang-Mills phase space onto a symplectic manifold, which is then flattened by utilizing the logarithm of the Yang-Mills action. This flattening process yields a phase-space probability distribution that is uniform and independent of the action. This novel distribution is defined by a path integral over the Yang-Mills group, weighted inversely by the absolute value of the action's determinant. This formulation is valid for all semi-classical states, including instantons, and offers a novel perspective on Yang-Mills theory.

We present a theoretical investigation into polarization anisotropies in the optical spectra of single wurtzite quantum wires. These structures are created by stacking a monolayer of GaN atop a two-dimensional GaN layer, which is itself grown on a sapphire substrate. Our findings indicate that the absorption spectrum exhibits significant dependence on the polarization angle, a feature that varies with the energy levels of the excitonic transitions. We attribute this anisotropy to the distinct orientations of the electric dipole moments associated with the excitons. Furthermore, the observed spectral features align well with the characteristics of the measured confocal microscope images.

Opponent modeling plays a crucial role in multi-agent systems, yet adapting pre-existing models to specific interactions remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a method for opponent modeling in negotiation dialogues that leverages related dialogue data to fine-tune a pre-established model. The approach involves identifying and retrieving similar dialogue instances from available datasets, followed by applying these samples to refine a model originally trained on the relevant domain. The efficacy of this proposed method is demonstrated through experiments on a negotiation dialogue corpus.

Balancing the sequence of assignments in online experiments is a fundamental issue across various fields, including clinical trials, A/B testing, and reinforcement learning. This paper introduces a novel approach to address this challenge by leveraging online matching algorithms. We propose a framework that models the assignment problem as bipartite matching, where one set of vertices represents experimental units and the other set represents pigeonholes—groups of experimental units characterized by specific covariates. By applying online matching methods to this structure, we generate balanced experimental sequences. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach by utilizing it to create a balanced design for a clinical trial. Furthermore, we establish a theoretical bound on the imbalance within the proposed design and validate our methodology through an A/B testing case study.

This study investigates the nonlinear statistical modeling of critical gravitational collapse, specifically focusing on the determination of the $\psi$ parameter. We employ a nonlinear regression approach to analyze the collapse of spherical dust clouds, utilizing a self-similar solution to the Einstein equations. This study introduces a comprehensive, harmonized dataset on the container shipping industry, offering a 100-year historical record from 1966 to 2020. The data encompasses global shipping rates, cargo volumes, and the prices of new and second-hand vessels, along with scrap rates and vessel construction metrics. By integrating information from various sources, we have created a unified database that enables researchers to analyze the industry's historical evolution and its responses to external shocks. This study presents a meta-level analysis of 12 anomaly detection algorithms, evaluating their performance across 14 datasets. We assessed these methods using 10 distinct metrics, including the F-measure, precision, recall, false positive rate, and execution time. Our findings indicate that the Isolation Forest algorithm consistently outperforms others, delivering superior results on 11 out of 14 datasets. Additionally, we examined the relationship between dataset characteristics and algorithm effectiveness, discovering that data dimensionality is the primary factor influencing performance.

This study examines the Rosenau equation, a nonlinear partial differential equation that serves as a generalization of the KdV equation, and introduces two distinct numerical approaches utilizing the discontinuous Galerkin finite element method. This study investigates the well-posedness of a coupled PDE system comprising the Euler equations for compressible flow and the Navier-Stokes equations for incompressible fluid, connected through a coupling operator. By applying the energy method to the abstract Cauchy problem associated with the system, we demonstrate that under specific constraints on the operator's properties, the resulting framework ensures uniform closed range and maximal $C_0$-semigroup well-posedness. These properties guarantee the existence, uniqueness, continuous dependence on initial conditions, and the derivation of an exponential decay estimate for the system's solution.

We present a theoretical investigation into the magnetic-field-driven crystallization of charged excitons (excitons polarons) within van der Waals heterostructures. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the formation of a crystalline state in this system is facilitated by the magnetic field-induced suppression of the kinetic energy of the center-of-mass motion.

This study introduces a novel approach to resolve the wide-band inverse scattering problem, which involves determining the spatial distribution of an object's magnetic permeability from measured electromagnetic fields across various frequencies and orientations. The method utilizes a neural network designed with inherent physical invariances, specifically rotation symmetry and gauge symmetry. The network's input consists of the time-domain magnetic field components across the full range of frequencies and angles, while the output represents the object's magnetic permeability. The proposed architecture integrates a Fourier-based feature extractor with a graph neural network to effectively capture both the global signal variations and local structural details. The network employs a novel fully equivariant design, ensuring that the output maintains rotational consistency with the input data. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through numerical experiments, which show that it surpasses existing techniques in terms of reconstruction accuracy.

Accelerated degradation testing (ADT) is a vital tool for estimating the reliability of new products. This study proposes an optimal, step-wise ADT strategy for products with two failure modes, where degradation follows a bivariate gamma process characterized by a positive correlation. The approach aims to minimize the variance of the maximum likelihood estimator for the model's correlation parameter, $\rho$, within a fixed timeframe. A key finding is that the optimal design necessitates a stepwise approach, utilizing a single design level for the first stage and multiple levels for subsequent stages. Furthermore, the optimal design levels are determined by solving a system of equations. To address the complexity of this system, a numerical method is introduced to calculate the optimal levels. The efficacy of this proposed design is demonstrated through a simulation study.

We investigate the triangular flow ($v_3$) in Au+Au and Cu+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 200$ GeV using the transport model AMPT. The $v_3$ values are calculated by applying the event mixing technique to the azimuthal distribution of charged particles. Our results indicate that $v_3$ exhibits a strong dependence on centrality, peaking in the most central collisions. Additionally, the ratio of $v_3$ between Au+Au and Cu+Au collisions shows a clear centrality dependence, which aligns with experimental data from STAR. This behavior is interpreted as arising from the interplay of initial geometry fluctuations and the medium's response.

This study investigates the polytropic behavior of solar wind plasma during the interaction between Interplanetary Coronal Mass Ejections (ICMEs) and High-speed Solar Wind Streams (HSSs). By analyzing data from the ACE and WIND spacecraft, we identified 11 ICME-HSS interaction events. We determined the plasma adiabatic index (gamma) using the polytropic relation, employing both the total plasma pressure and thermal pressure. Our results indicate that the plasma behaves isentropically when total plasma pressure is used, whereas non-isentropic behavior emerges when thermal pressure is applied. This discrepancy suggests that non-thermal contributions to the total plasma pressure are significant during ICME-HSS interactions. Furthermore, we observed that the plasma isentropic nature is disrupted by the presence of magnetic reconnection.

The random waypoint (RWP) model is a widely adopted method for simulating node movement in wireless ad-hoc networks. This paper examines the stochastic properties of the RWP model, specifically analyzing the statistical distributions of nodes' waypoints and speeds. Furthermore, we derive the mean square displacement for RWP nodes and present simulation findings illustrating these theoretical results.

This study examines $K^+K^-$ pairs within the STAR experiment at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 200$ GeV, utilizing data from central Au+Au and $p$+Pb collisions. The analysis focuses on the effective mass interval near $2m_K$ and the transverse momentum ($p_T$) range of 0.5 to 2.0 GeV/$c$. The findings reveal that the effective mass spectra for $p$+Pb and Au+Au collisions are nearly identical, showing no indications of low-mass excess or a dip near the threshold. Furthermore, the $p_T$ distributions for both collision systems are consistent with a single-exponential fit.

The microscopic collective inertial mass, a fundamental component of the inertia tensor, is essential for analyzing nuclear collective motion. This paper investigates how the effective in-medium nucleon mass influences the microscopic collective inertial mass. We demonstrate that the dependence of this mass on the mass parameter $\kappa$ of the effective mass follows the same trend as the moment of inertia. Furthermore, we examine the impact of the effective mass on the microscopic collective inertia associated with the wobbling mode in the $^{182}$W nucleus. Our findings indicate that the moment of inertia linked to the wobbling mode exhibits a similar behavior to the corresponding collective inertial mass.

The Abstraction Reasoning Corpus (ARC) serves as a benchmark for assessing artificial general intelligence (AGI) capabilities by utilizing a dataset of human-constructed problems that are brief yet challenging to resolve algorithmically. ARC problems consist of grid-based images where the task involves inferring a function mapping an input image to an output image based on preceding examples. While previous research has addressed AGI challenges through various lenses, this study uniquely approaches the problem from a graph-theoretic perspective. We introduce a graph abstraction method designed to extract relevant information from ARC images, thereby reducing the search space for potential solutions. Furthermore, we develop a novel search algorithm that leverages this abstraction to efficiently identify solution functions. Experimental results indicate that our approach successfully solves 100 out of 200 ARC problems, achieving a 50% success rate.

This study examines the discontinuity characteristics of smooth solutions to scalar conservation laws featuring discontinuous flux. We establish that the solution's second derivative exhibits fractional integrability with an exponent of $-1/2$ along the discontinuity curve. Furthermore, the paper derives a fractional trace theorem for the solution's derivatives, revealing that although the second derivative is discontinuous across the curve, its discontinuity is not severe enough to prevent fractional integrability.
